The forum opened in Xi'an, capital city of northwest China's Shaanxi Province, on Tuesday. Themed "High-quality Belt and Road Cooperation Empowering Modernization and Mutual Learning among Civilizations," these forums aim to pool global wisdom and promote new development of Belt and Road cooperation with higher quality and at a higher level. (Xinhua/Li Yibo) XI'AN, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 and the 4th Silk Road (Xi'an) International Communication Forum opened in Xi'an, capital city of northwest China's Shaanxi Province, on Tuesday. Themed "High-quality Belt and Road Cooperation Empowering Modernization and Mutual Learning among Civilizations," these forums aim to pool global wisdom and promote new development of Belt and Road cooperation with higher quality and at a higher level. More than 300 diplomats, think tank experts, journalists, cultural and tourism experts, and business representatives from over 50 countries and regions are attending these forums to engage in exchanges and discussions. In his address, Zhao Gang, deputy secretary of the Shaanxi Provincial Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and governor of Shaanxi, said Shaanxi has in recent years deeply integrated itself into the broader pattern of Belt and Road cooperation. Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua News Agency, said that over the past 13 years, Belt and Road cooperation has grown from a vision into tangible and visible cooperation projects, making positive contributions to enhancing friendship between China and partner countries and promoting the economic and social development of partner countries. As the lead of the Initiators Council of the Belt and Road Studies Network (BRSN), Xinhua is ready to work with domestic and international colleagues to deepen research and interpretation of the connotations of high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, showcase the fruitful achievements of partner countries in advancing modernization and mutual learning among civilizations, and gather strong momentum for high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, Lyu said. The BRSN has continued to expand its influence since its establishment seven years ago. At the opening ceremony, four new member institutions, namely BRICS International Forum, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Manas National Academy of the Kyrgyz Republic, and the Development Strategy Centre, Uzbekistan were presented with signing documents. A think tank report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation" was, meanwhile, released globally in both Chinese and English. The forums are co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency, the CPC Shaanxi Provincial Committee and the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government. ■ This photo taken on Nov. 10, 2026 shows a scene of the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 and the 4th Silk Road (Xi'an) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province. item.title: China's import expo wraps up with record intended deals, global debuts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, with the value of one-year intended deals reaching a record high of 85.45 billion U.S. dollars, up 2.3 percent from the previous edition, according to Xiao Lu, an official with the CIIE Bureau. This year's expo attracted a record 4,142 exhibitors, and its business exhibition area reached a record 370,000 square meters. For the first time, the number of participating Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders exceeded 300. The six-day event also featured a record 485 exhibits making their global, Asian or China debuts, up from 461 last year. U.S. exhibitors had the largest exhibition area among participating countries and regions for the eighth consecutive year, occupying over 50,000 square meters. Free exhibition space for the least developed countries increased by 17 percent this year, enabling broader participation. First held in 2018 as the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, the CIIE is part of China's efforts to expand imports and offers global businesses a platform to showcase products and connect with Chinese buyers. Among the technological highlights this year, U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm showcased the world's first 6G terminal prototype outside a laboratory setting, while German engineering giant Bosch made the global debut of an AI-powered home climate control system that optimizes temperature and energy use. Consumer innovations also drew attention. Canadian sportswear brand lululemon made the global debut of a running vest designed for cold weather, set to launch first in China on Dec. 8. The CIIE also served as a platform for emerging innovators. This year's innovation incubation section featured 633 projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. The ninth expo brought together 51 trade delegations and over 700 sub-delegations, while the number of registered visitors exceeded 470,000, surpassing last year's figure, according to Xiao. China has remained the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years, importing more than 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for expanding imports and continuing to host the CIIE, underscoring the expo's role in China's broader opening-up agenda. With the CIIE set to hold its 10th edition next year, preparations are already underway, with 143 companies and institutions signed up for the 2027 edition and over 100,000 square meters of exhibition space already booked, according to the bureau. ■

item.title: Russia, Ukraine, U.S. conclude 1st day of trilateral talks, with negotiations to continue Wednesday
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
ABU DHABI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Russia, Ukraine and the United States concluded the first day of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on Tuesday after nearly four hours of discussions. The talks are set to continue on Wednesday. The talks are the first trilateral meeting among the three countries since February. The Russian delegation is headed by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky and includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov, among other officials. U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the U.S. delegation. According to Interfax-Ukraine, citing Ukrainian presidential communications adviser Dmytro Lytvyn, the Ukrainian delegation includes Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, and Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office, as well as other officials. In opening remarks, Medinsky expressed hope that the meeting would help advance peace in the interests of the people of Russia and Ukraine, and Umerov said the latest round of talks aimed to achieve lasting peace. Ahead of the trilateral talks, the Ukrainian team met with representatives of Britain, France, Germany and Italy, as well as officials from NATO and the European Commission. The meeting was also attended by U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Following the first day of talks, Ukrainian and U.S. officials described the discussions as constructive and productive. Later in the day, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on social media platform X that the trilateral talks were "constructive and quite substantive," with the participants discussing possible humanitarian steps, including the release of prisoners, which he described as a priority. He noted that the discussions also focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and mechanisms to ensure their long-term effectiveness, as well as steps toward de-escalation. Zelensky added that the talks would continue Wednesday, stressing that the main goal was to "truly bring peace closer." Speaking after a meeting of Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers in Paris, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks as "very productive," saying the trilateral format should eventually be expanded to include European partners. On Tuesday, Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 162 drones and one ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, while Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces intercepted and destroyed 155 Ukrainian drones. Those military claims could not be independently verified.■

item.title: Xinhua think tank report highlights high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
This photo shows copies of the think tank report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation." (Xinhua/Jin Liangkuai) XI'AN, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A national high-level think tank released a report on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy on Tuesday. The report, titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation," was released by Xinhua Institute, a think tank affiliated with Xinhua News Agency, at the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 & the 4th Silk Road (XI'AN) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, capital of northwest China's Shaanxi Province. Consisting of three chapters, the report showcases the concrete practices of Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) cooperation in building an open world economy, analyzes the serious challenges facing economic globalization, and explains the contemporary significance of BRI cooperation in following the historical trend and opening broad prospects for the world economy. According to the report, high-quality BRI cooperation exemplifies China's commitment to opening-up as a fundamental national policy and to a mutually beneficial opening-up strategy. The report noted that BRI cooperation has consistently upheld the principles of extensive consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits; embraced open, green, and clean cooperation; and pursued high standards, sustainability, and better lives for people. By steering economic globalization toward greater openness, inclusiveness, balance, and benefits for all, the BRI contributes Chinese approaches and insights to the building of an open world economy, it said. The report stated that the rise of anti-globalization sentiment, the spread of unilateralism and protectionism, weak global growth drivers, lagging governance, and uneven development are realities that must be confronted. At the same time, economic globalization reflects the objective requirements of the development of productive forces, and its historical direction cannot be reversed. Countries are more interdependent than ever, creating major opportunities to address global problems through openness and cooperation. Amid these changes, China's approach is to consider both domestic and international conditions, expand high-standard opening-up, and build global development partnerships. In this way, it seeks to turn challenges into a powerful impetus for an open world economy and realize a vision of inclusive development and mutual benefit for all, said the report. BRI cooperation keeps pace with the times, meets development needs, and responds to people's aspirations. It takes concrete action against decoupling, supply chain disruption, and bloc confrontation, using connectivity to remove barriers and facilitate economic flows, according to the report. At this new stage of history, BRI cooperation is moving from major corridors to extensive networks. Driven by digitalization and the green transition, it is deepening institutional opening-up and promoting collaborative innovation to make global development more balanced, inclusive, and sustainable, the report said. Looking ahead, the report stressed that BRI cooperation will provide stronger support for an open world economy, bring renewed vitality to global economic governance, reinforce the foundations of a community with a shared future for humanity, and open brighter prospects for world peace and development. The full report, comprising approximately 18,000 Chinese characters, was released globally in both Chinese and English through relevant websites, journals, social media, and other platforms. ■ A participant reads a copy of a report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation," at the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 & the 4th Silk Road (XI'AN) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Nov. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Yibo)

item.title: China hands over remains of U.S. airmen found along WWII Hump Route
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
A document confirming the transfer of the U.S. airmen remains found along Hump Route is signed, witnessed by Chinese and American representatives, during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Bingjie) CHENGDU, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese honor guards walked forward, carrying a box containing human remains. U.S. honor guards stepped up to receive it and carefully placed an American national flag over the box. The box held eight bone fragments recovered from a glacier more than 5,000 meters above sea level. The remains, believed to belong to U.S. airmen who went missing along the Hump Route during World War II (WWII), had lain in the mountains for more than 80 years. At the handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, on Tuesday, He Jiang, director of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Archives, and U.S. Navy Captain Colin Alexander Eliot, a forensic expert with the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA), signed a document confirming the transfer, witnessed by Chinese and American representatives. The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, which was established after Japanese forces occupied Myanmar in 1942, cutting off the Yunnan-Myanmar road, China's last major overland supply link to the outside world. Stretching from the state of Assam in northeastern India to Kunming in southwest China, the air corridor across the Himalayas became a vital lifeline for Allied supplies supporting China's resistance against Japanese aggression from 1942 to 1945. The route crossed snow-covered mountains, deep gorges, glaciers and tropical forests. Violent air currents, low air pressure, hail and freezing conditions posed constant risks to aircraft flying through the region. It became known as the "death route." More than 1,000 Chinese and American aircrew members lost their lives along the route. With the high mountains and glaciers making searches exceptionally difficult, many of their remains have never been recovered. The fragments handed over on Tuesday were found by a search team organized by Jianchuan Museum, a privately run museum in Sichuan, during expeditions to the glaciers of Nyingchi in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The searchers trekked through primeval forests and waded across rushing rivers, taking care to avoid bears in the mountains and deadly hazards on the glaciers. After repeated searches, they finally located the remains. China and the United States have cooperated in searching for American military personnel missing during WWII since the 1970s. Both Chinese authorities and civilian groups have contributed to those efforts. An official with the general office of the Central Military Commission, who attended the ceremony, said the joint efforts to recover the remains of missing U.S. servicemen were a testament to the two countries' history of fighting side by side against Japanese fascism during WWII. China has long supported the search on humanitarian grounds and is willing to continue practical cooperation with the United States in this field, the official said, adding that such efforts could contribute positively to building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. "These remains bear witness to the war against fascism and carry the history of the Chinese and American peoples fighting aggression together," said Fan Jianchuan, curator of Jianchuan Museum. "They also remind us to strengthen cooperation and make new contributions to world peace." Addressing the ceremony, Eliot spoke of the shared wartime history that the remains represent. "The remains before us represent a defining historical moment when Americans, compelled by duty to defend against aggression, stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the people of China to fight that very same threat," he said. Following the ceremony, Chinese and U.S. representatives visited the Hall of the Heroes of the Flying Tigers, which commemorates the Flying Tigers and other American servicemen who assisted China during WWII. Through wartime artifacts and other displays, the exhibition documents the history of Chinese and American cooperation against Japanese aggression. It has received more than 10 million visitors since opening over two decades ago. The airmen's identities have yet to be established. After the remains reach the United States, the DPAA will conduct DNA testing, examine historical evidence, and compare military records. Families will be notified only after identification is confirmed. ■ Chinese honor guards handover the box containing the U.S. airmen remains found along Hump Route during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Bingjie) U.S. honor guards receive the box containing the U.S. airmen remains found along Hump Route during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Bingjie)

item.title: China's import expo tells a larger story of openness, shared opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
* The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors and featured more than 480 global, Asian or China debuts. Organizers reported 85.45 billion U.S. dollars in intended deals. * Greek financial news outlet Business Daily described the CIIE as an "importathon" -- a blend of "import" and "marathon," suggesting a sustained drive to bring goods into the Chinese market. * John Ross, a former director of economic and business policy for the mayor of London, told Xinhua that China was not seeking a trade surplus but rather greater openness in world trade. For foreign exporters, he called the CIIE "the best export opportunity that you've got in the world." SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- In 2018, German warehouse-equipment maker Jungheinrich showcased a German-made forklift at China's inaugural import expo. This year, it unveiled an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted warehouse-planning tool developed partly in China -- a sign of the country's growing role as a source of innovation for global businesses, not just a vast market. The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors and featured more than 480 global, Asian or China debuts. Organizers reported 85.45 billion U.S. dollars in intended deals. For decades, China's manufacturing strengths have drawn foreign companies, many of which have used the country as a base to serve global markets. In 2025, foreign-invested enterprises accounted for 27 percent of China's exports and 16 percent of its trade surplus, according to official figures. Shanghai has long been a major gateway for China's exports. In 2025, its port recorded total container throughput of more than 55 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), retaining its position as the world's busiest container port for the 16th consecutive year. The city has also become a gateway for foreign businesses seeking access to China's import market. Since 2018, it has hosted the CIIE, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, described by Chinese officials as "an international public good shared by the world." For Ethiopian economist Alemayehu Geda, China's expanding import market offers an opportunity for African producers to move beyond raw-material exports. China is "not only encouraging exporters as was traditionally the case, but also importers into China," the Addis Ababa University professor said. Greek financial news outlet Business Daily described the CIIE as an "importathon" -- a blend of "import" and "marathon," suggesting a sustained drive to bring goods into the Chinese market. Nepalese entrepreneur Shankar Koirala has witnessed those opportunities grow over six CIIE appearances. His booth expanded from nine to 72 square meters. Each handmade cashmere scarf bears its maker's signature. Together, the products connect Chinese buyers with more than 600 artisan families in Nepal. "When we didn't know where to promote our products, the CIIE gave us a platform," Koirala said. John Ross, a former director of economic and business policy for the mayor of London, told Xinhua that China was not seeking a trade surplus but rather greater openness in world trade. For foreign exporters, he called the CIIE "the best export opportunity that you've got in the world." China imported more than 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. At this year's CIIE, free exhibition space for the least developed countries increased by 17 percent, while the Asia-Africa products zone was upgraded. Beyond the exhibition halls, China has expanded preferential access to its market. Since May 1, eligible imports from all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations have enjoyed zero tariffs. That morning, 24 tonnes of South African apples became the first shipment cleared under the policy in Shenzhen. When China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, its annual goods trade stood at about 500 billion U.S. dollars. By 2025, it exceeded 6 trillion dollars. China's role as a buyer has grown as well: imports from more than 130 countries and regions increased last year, customs data showed. China has also taken steps in support of the multilateral trading system. In 2025, it announced it would not seek new special and differential treatment in current or future WTO negotiations. This year, it pledged 1.1 million dollars to WTO programs that support developing and least-developed economies. These efforts come as the multilateral trading system faces mounting challenges. The WTO's World Trade Report 2026 says global trade policy and the organization face "the most serious and sustained disruptions" since the multilateral trading system emerged 80 years ago. Addressing the opening ceremony of the CIIE, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called on countries to share market opportunities and promote balanced trade by making the economic pie bigger together. He also urged deeper investment cooperation, innovation and the removal of trade barriers. For French yeast maker Lesaffre, making that pie bigger through innovation can bring benefits well beyond China. At its Shanghai industrial baking center, the company tests processes for customers across Asia-Pacific. Solutions refined in China can be applied elsewhere, an approach the company calls the "China fulcrum effect." "A solution validated on these lines in China can be scaled for customers across Asia-Pacific," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. In cosmetics, French group L'Oréal joined forces with Chinese company Nanomed to develop a Lancome skincare device. Displayed at the 2025 CIIE, the device had reached markets in more than 20 countries and regions by July 2026. In telecommunications, U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm showcased a sixth-generation (6G) communications terminal prototype following tests with China Mobile and Chinese telecommunications equipment maker ZTE. The CIIE also served as a platform for emerging innovators. This year's innovation incubation section featured 633 projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. Taken together, these examples point to an evolution beyond unveiling imported products and technologies. International companies are increasingly developing new technologies and manufacturing innovative products in China, drawing on local expertise to serve both Chinese and overseas markets -- part of what has come to be known as "China Opportunity 2.0." Shanghai's own history offers a wider perspective on this evolution. The city became home to China's first pilot free trade zone in 2013. This July, representatives of 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which will be headquartered in the city. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China next week. The theme of this year's summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," while China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation. In 2025, APEC's 21 member economies were home to 3 billion people and accounted for 61.6 percent of global real GDP. The gathering carries historical resonance. Shanghai hosted APEC leaders in October 2001, just weeks before China's WTO accession, at a meeting that marked a fresh start for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the new century. At the 2014 Beijing summit, leaders endorsed a roadmap toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, an initiative that APEC trade ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing in May. Back in Shanghai, 49 companies and institutions signed up on Nov. 6 for the CIIE's 10th edition in 2027. Among them was German optics group ZEISS, which this year showcased a new-generation intraocular lens developed by its joint venture in China. For Martin Fischer, president and CEO of ZEISS Greater China, China is not only the company's largest market globally, but also a vital source of innovation. "The time it takes to turn an idea into a prototype is shorter in China than anywhere else," he said. (Video reporters: Zhu Cong, Hong Liang, Sun Qing; Video editors: Yang Zeyi, Roger Lott, Zhang Mocheng) ■

item.title: China's foreign trade growth picks up pace on stellar imports, booming AI demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade in goods maintained strong growth momentum in the first 10 months of 2026, with imports posting especially robust gains and booming artificial intelligence (AI) demand lifting exports of electronic components, official data showed Tuesday. Total imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year to 44.81 trillion yuan (about 6.67 trillion U.S. dollars) over the period, accelerating from 18.8 percent in the first nine months, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Imports surged 23.6 percent, while exports rose 17.6 percent during the January-October period. China's foreign trade has kept up its momentum this year, showing greater resilience and vitality, said Lyu Daliang, director of the GAC's Department of Statistics and Analysis. Both imports and exports have now posted double-digit growth for six consecutive months through October, the customs data showed. In October alone, goods trade expanded 31.2 percent. Notably, imports have been a standout feature this year. "In the first 10 months, China's imports from more than 150 countries and regions recorded growth. Imports from ASEAN, Latin America and Africa all reached record highs for the same period," Lyu said. "China's vast market continued to offer 'China opportunities' to the world." On the export side, mechanical and electrical products played a prominent role with a 25.2 percent increase over the period, accounting for 64.7 percent of total exports, up 3.9 percentage points from a year earlier. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, said multiple factors kept export growth elevated in October, noting that the global AI investment boom continued to push up prices of chips and other electronic components and computer parts, driving strong growth in export value. Moreover, domestic manufacturing upgrades in recent years have also enhanced the competitiveness of new energy vehicles and high-tech products, Wang said. Smart and green products were among the fastest-growing categories. Exports of integrated circuits and memory components surged 101.9 percent and 132.5 percent, respectively, while 3D printers, digital cameras and industrial robots rose 104.8 percent, 41.4 percent and 17.8 percent. Exports of China's "new three" -- electric vehicles, photovoltaic products and lithium batteries -- grew 46.5 percent, electric motorcycles and bicycles rose 33.3 percent, and wind turbines and their components gained 19.7 percent. By trading partner, China's trade with ASEAN grew 24.2 percent in the first 10 months, while trade with the European Union rose 8.5 percent and trade with the United States expanded 6.3 percent. Trade with Belt and Road participating countries grew 18.5 percent over the same period. Looking ahead, experts believe the strong exports will extend through to the end of the year. As the AI cycle remains in an upswing, China will continue to benefit as a global hub of electronics supply chains, Zhang Di, a macro analyst at China Galaxy Securities, said. The ongoing global green and low-carbon transition, combined with China's rising competitiveness in mechanical equipment, will sustain strong growth in new energy vehicles, ships and other transport machinery, Zhang added. ■

item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity. ■
